newsitem.title: USA: Fed could add reserves or take no action - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Fed could add reserves or take no action - analysts.

text.p: The Federal Reserve could add a small amount of temporary reserves to the banking system through system repurchases or refrain from action altogether, analysts said.
"There's a chance of a small system," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and economist at Dean Witter Securities.

Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co said she calculated that the Fed had "a small add need" but with Federal funds trading below the 5-1/2 percent target, she was "leaning toward no Fed, with the possibility of another small system repurchase like they did yesterday."
On Tuesday, the Fed added $1.420 billion in temporary reserves to the banking system through an overnight system repurchase operation.
Federal funds were trading at 5-7/16 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/2 percent target for the rate, in early dealings.
"I show a $1.0 billion to a $1.5 billion add need but funds are comfortable," said Thrapp.

Analysts at Standard & Poor's MMS said their calculations also show a small add need but said "(Treasury) deposits at the Fed remain relatively low ($4.76 billion on Tuesday), which could keep the desk sidelined."
